The decision to treat an element as a leaf (string value) or as a nested object is based on whether the element has non-whitespace text, rather than on whether it has child elements. According to the spec, an element with child elements must always become a JSON object, ignoring any direct text. The code instead checks `child.text.strip()` first, so elements that have both text and child elements incorrectly produce a string value and skip their children. Additionally, leaf elements with no text (or only whitespace) are omitted entirely instead of being assigned an empty string, because the code only sets a value if the nested dict is non-empty. This also causes parent elements whose children are all empty leaves to be omitted. While the provided usage example works by coincidence, the code fails for other valid inputs described in the task.
